name: Dark Zurich
ability_definition: The ability to see under low-light conditions.

task_realism.reasoning: Recognizing and localizing road users, signs, buildings and road layout in real nighttime urban driving footage closely mirrors a core workplace use of night vision: night driving and patrol. It omits other low-light settings such as indoor dim spaces, rural or unlit terrain, aviation, and maritime work.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Evaluation uses static single frames with no temporal continuity, no real-time constraint, and no consequences for errors. The standard protocol is unsupervised adaptation from labeled daytime Cityscapes, so scores partly reflect domain-transfer skill rather than seeing in the dark. The held-out test server with real night images is a strength.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It spans twilight to full night and 19 semantic classes, but only in urban driving scenes with artificial street lighting from one region. Near-total darkness, non-urban environments, and fine-detail detection of small or distant objects are underrepresented, so it measures a meaningful but narrow slice of low-light perception.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are genuine nighttime camera images, which is realistic. The output is a dense pixel-level segmentation map, a reasonable readout of scene understanding but not the form in which workers use night vision (detect, identify, act). Labels are fine-grained and not forced-choice.

transferability_reasoning: Dark Zurich tests perception on real nighttime images with dense, verifiable labels, which gives it solid realism and format relevance for night-driving-style tasks. Its transfer to the general ability to see in low light is limited by its narrow urban-driving scope, static-frame evaluation, and a protocol that confounds night perception with day-to-night domain adaptation.

2020.model_or_system: MGCDA (Map-Guided Curriculum Domain Adaptation, RefineNet ResNet-101 backbone)
2020.metric: mIoU (%) over 19 Cityscapes classes on Dark Zurich-test
2020.human_reference: General adult workforce who must perceive scene content at night, such as drivers, delivery workers and security staff. The reference is people with normal vision viewing real nighttime urban and suburban driving imagery.

2021.metric: mIoU (%) over 19 classes on Dark Zurich-test
2021.human_reference: General adult population (e.g., typical drivers or pedestrians) perceiving real nighttime urban street scenes

2022.model_or_system: Refign-HRDA (Refign applied on top of HRDA, with Cityscapes-pretrained initialization)
2022.human_reference: General adult population, specifically typical drivers or people who must perceive and interpret urban street scenes at night (Night Vision is a general perceptual ability, not a specialist skill)

2023.model_or_system: CISS (Condition-Invariant Semantic Segmentation, built on HRDA)
2023.metric: mIoU (%) on Dark Zurich-test, Cityscapes→Dark Zurich unsupervised domain adaptation
2023.human_reference: General adult population with normal vision, e.g. drivers and workers who must recognize scene contents in low light. This is a basic perceptual ability, not a specialist skill.

2024.metric: mIoU (%) over 19 classes on Dark Zurich-test
2024.human_reference: General adult workforce who must see and recognize scene content under low light, such as drivers, security staff and outdoor workers. Reference: the median sighted adult identifying and localizing road, sidewalk, vehicles, people, signs, buildings, vegetation and sky in urban night scenes.
